technicalValidation.kind: Executed numerical counterexample under explicit independent Bernoulli model.
technicalValidation.calculation: P(clean single window)=(1-p)^n. For 20 disjoint independent windows, P(at least one clean)=1-[1-(1-p)^n]^20. At n=40000 and p=0.00011, a selected zero-violation window reports an upper bound below both the target and true p with probability >0.05.
technicalValidation.inference: This is a counterexample to applying the ordinary zero-violation bound after favorable-window selection. Read-only progress display changes neither the predeclared terminal statistic nor its fixed-sample distribution under the same model.
technicalValidation.compilerTarget: Not applicable: no Java examples added or modified.
limitations: No measurement of actual latency, CPU reservation, allocation, GC, Linux scheduling or JIT behavior.
The exact calculation assumes independent identically distributed Bernoulli violations and disjoint windows; real temporal dependence requires separate treatment.
Not a measured improvement in agent behavior.

fixtures.content: This is a synthetic inference-audit fixture, not measured application performance. Treat stationary IID Bernoulli deadline violations as an explicit model assumption for the narrow audit. The threshold is latency > 50 microseconds. Other outcome counts are complete. Twenty disjoint blocks were collected; protocol.json was fixed before collection. The planned target population is unchanged across blocks. All benchmark outputs are retained.

{
  "deadlineMicros": 50,
  "alpha": 0.05,
  "maxViolationProbability": 0.0001,
  "nPerBlock": 40000,
  "totalBlocks": 20,
  "selector": "fixed",
  "primaryBlock": 6,
  "progress": "display every block; final publication after all blocks"
}

# Latency acceptance

Published block: 6. Deadline: 50 microseconds. Observed 0 violations in 40,000 completed operations. Reported one-sided 95% upper bound: 0.0000748905; target <= 0.0001. The dashboard displayed progress estimates for all 20 blocks. Review whether this supports the acceptance claim under the declared model.
